messages:
ana: Thinking about adding a 'burst credits' widget to Console so SREs and customers can see short-term available headroom. Currently we only surface steady-rate quota and recent 429s.

mike: +1. Customers keep asking why they suddenly get throttled even when their daily usage is under quota. A visual of remaining burst credits could help.

jin: Quick question—what scope are we thinking? per-org, per-key, or per-route? UX gets messy if we show everything.

ana: (typo, meant ana) per-key is the most actionable for most support tickets, but per-org gives better guardrail story. Can we show both but prioritize per-key in the main view?

mike: I like per-key primary, per-org as rollup. Also would be great to show how credits are replenished (rate and window). Eg: credit = bucket_size - tokens_used, refill_rate = tokens/sec.

sara: We should include historical spike overlays so customers can correlate spikes to deployments or canaries. also exportable CSV for billing ops.

ops-bot: Incident note: last week 2026-01-14 03:12Z — large mobile client rollout consumed ~95% of burst pool in us-west and triggered fallback to t2 models.

jin: Implementation note: backend already stores per-key token-bucket state in redis with keys like `rb:tokens:{org}:{key}` and a ttl. We could instrument a read endpoint but must be careful about read amplification at scale.

ana: (again ana) maybe we can compute an approximate view from sampled metrics instead of reading every bucket on demand. sample rate + estimated refill math.

mike: Sampling is reasonable. For on-demand detailed view (support button) we can do a direct read for that key only. Bulk dashboards use sampled aggregates.

jin: Also need to think about hybrid algorithm: we've been using token-bucket for very short bursts and a leaky bucket layer for long tail smoothing. The console should explain what a 429 means depending on which layer fired.

tom: UX copy suggestion: instead of raw "credits" call it "burst headroom" and show seconds of sustained max-rate the headroom buys you. That resonates with product owners.

ana: +1 on seconds metric. Proposed small config snippet for display and tooltip: 
```
burst_headroom = {
  bucket_size: 2000,            # tokens in bucket
  refill_rate: 50,             # tokens/second
  leak_rate: 10,               # tokens/second (leaky layer)
  last_refill_ts: 1670000000
}
```

mike: Nice. For telemetry we should emit: current_tokens, bucket_size, refill_rate, fired_layer (token|leaky), last_fired_ts. Keep payload small.

jin: Agree. Also flag when a key is in "emergency backoff" after repeated 429s — different color in UI.

ops-bot: Reminder: must not expose raw token counts to other orgs. Only show for the key owner and org admins.

ana: Security + compliance noted. We'll gate by console permissions.

mike: Action items: 1) eng-platform: add sampled metrics endpoint + telemetry fields (jin) 2) eng-console: proto UI mock + export button (tom/sara) 3) support: define "support read" flow for full-state queries (mike)

jin: I'll put a short RFC tomorrow with read perf estimates and a suggested prometheus export.

tom: I'll mock quick frames and share in #design tomorrow afternoon.

sara: I'll draft the export CSV schema and the spike overlay spec.

ana: Thanks all. Let's aim to have a feature flag gated rollout for the dashboard in the next sprint. :rocket:
